findings.finding: The checker never reads several record members that carry an owner decision or a binding rule, so check accepts a record that contradicts them. Each was probed as one mutation of the published records through check_set, which returned no refusal: the release-pinned local CA kept as an online software key on the host, issuing KUBERNETES_PROXY_SERVER_MTLS too, or allowed in the API server's client trust (Q-LHA-16 (2); B-LHA-2); the per-run cluster CA made at step 13 or needing a new key or token (B-LHA-2; MON-LHA-B2); T2's order with the drop manifest signed first (runbook step 12; Q-LHA-2); the bundles installed after the revocation or their digests not in the envelope (MON-LHA3-1-2); the LIVE_MANIFEST drop target set ACTIVE while liveLauncher.state is WAITING, after which check_drop accepts a drop manifest that lists the live manifest (design section 6: only once CONF-LIVE-005/006 close); CAMPAIGN_PROXY_CLIENT_MTLS issuedAt set to STEP_8, which skips the T2 drop-target check; the drop directory mode 0777 or the staging directory not root-owned (B-LHA-4); the export unit run as OPERATOR_UID, contradicting privilegedActions (B-LHA-1); custody.json written at step 13 (design section 6); the custom image's root on XFS without verity, or imageDigest not recomputed off host (Q-LHA-15); an automatic restart inside the lease (Q-LHA-8). A one-leaf-at-a-time sweep accepted 188 of 312 custody, 165 of 314 launcher and 346 of 705 recipe changes; many are placeholders or prose, the ones above are not. Separately, check_recipe indexes the profile rows by name without a presence check: renaming the SELINUX_ENFORCING or REVIEWED_EXACT_BINARY_POLICY row raises KeyError, which the CLI prints as 'refused: KeyError' (not a stated rule) and which explain(), and so replay, does not catch, so no vector can record it. The oracle's own record assertions pin some published values, but the README presents check as the records' checker.
findings.requiredChange: Add model checks, each with a refusal vector, at least for: (a) localCa: issues exactly the two T2 leaves, offline generation, a token with a sealed backup, per-release rotation, never in the client trust; (b) clusterCa: made at step 7 on the node, issues only KUBERNETES_PROXY_SERVER_MTLS at step 8 with admin, no new key or token, its trust path equal to the proxy/operator host's cluster-CA trust; (c) T1 at step 10 after the freeze and T2 at step 12 in the runbook's order; bundles and revocation refreshed in T1 and installed at step 10 before the revocation, with their digests in the envelope; (d) the live-manifest targets' state tied to liveLauncher.state, and both local-CA leaves issued in T2; (e) the drop and staging directories' owner, group and mode, the trigger units' runsAs and command equal to privilegedActions, and custody.json at step 10; (f) the custom image's EXT4_WITH_VERITY root with usr on it, imageDigest from the read-only build disk and recomputed off host, and no automatic restart inside the lease; (g) a missing profile row refused by a named rule, with explain() mapping KeyError and TypeError to refusals as main() does.

findings.finding: Every schema pattern is anchored '^...$' and the model applies it with re.fullmatch, which agrees with ECMA-262, the draft 2020-12 semantics. Python's jsonschema validator uses re.search, where '$' also matches before a final line feed: on the drop manifest, planSha256, instance, bootId and validFrom with a trailing line feed are valid to jsonschema and refused by the model. Over the 228 published, positive and negative documents the two agree exactly.
